quote: It would be worse than finding rabbit fossils in the pre-Cambrian.
content: The prohibition is on complex, coordinated adaptation appearing from scratch in one generation by mutation: "the biological machinery necessary to generate electricity; the biological adaptations necessary to avoid being harmed... finely tuned control." Horizontal transfer imports machinery that evolved gradually in another lineage, and endosymbiosis imports a whole organism that evolved gradually; the aphid's carotenoid genes were built by selection in fungi. These are routes by which the theory lets complexity move between lineages. They are not exceptions to its ban on complexity appearing from nowhere. Neo-Darwinism absorbed them without auxiliary hypotheses because it never prohibited them.

quote: And yet they have no idea of what the theory of evolutionary biology permits and prohibits.
content: Fable's data are the essay's thesis. If acceptance of evolution tracks religiosity and political identity rather than understanding (Miller, Scott & Okamoto 2006), then it is belief worn as attire: professed for the sake of belonging and uncoupled from what the theory prohibits. Shtulman found that most adults, including those who accepted evolution, held the "transformational" misconception, and that accepting the theory did not predict understanding it (Shtulman 2006). That is the essay's claim that people who "very definitely believe in evolution" have "no idea of what the theory... permits and prohibits." The essay offered no cure by which literacy removes the attire; it said what attire is. Kahan's literate partisans are well-tailored, and the essay would expect them to be.

quote: Their devastating critiques consist purely of comparisons to apocalyptic literature, rather than, say, known laws which prohibit such an outcome.
content: The asymmetry is the ordinary one between claiming something is impossible and claiming it is possible. The critics called strongly superhuman AI "pseudoscience," which is a claim that it cannot happen, and that claim needs a bound. The essay's position was that nobody had one, and nearly twenty years later nobody does. Storm is ruled out by a known result, that complex adaptations accumulate through selection over many generations. Nothing comparable rules out minds more capable than ours. The history since has gone against the critics: systems built without any finished theory of cognition now outperform the best humans at Go, at protein-structure prediction and at olympiad mathematics. The critics' devastating critiques were literary, as the essay said.
